trust_decision.summary: Access to privileged Host API methods (settings/credentials planes, llm.discoverModels, agentPreset authoring, host.openPath/pickDirectory) is decided by whether the client-supplied Host header names a loopback authority, in the /api fetch handler of dsh-client-connection; every other Host method (including session.prompt) has no identity check at all, only the Host/Origin rebinding fence.

landing_point.why: The PRIVILEGED_METHODS loopback check in the /api route is the only per-method authority decision; an engineer told 'auth bypass in the local HTTP control-plane API' searches for the gate and finds the Host-header-only loopback test here.

fix_sites.entry_point: HTTP POST /api/<method> (API Proxy methods, all of them)
public service API ctx.connection.isTrustedRequest (used by sibling Web routes such as the WS upgrade)
HTTP POST /api/<endpoint> claimed by a ctx.connection.rpc.intercept interceptor (Typert Remote unary)
HTTP POST <channel>/<endpoint> for any channel registered via ctx.connection.rpc.handle
fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level public API (generic channel registry; no src caller at pin)

fix_sites.entry_point: new BrowserAuth (launch token, signed authority-bound cookie, credential-store secret) used by all of the above
Typert Remote unary calls on /api via intercept (authority option dropped)
HTTP GET / and configured index path (token exchange / cookie gate before index HTML)
webserver fallback seat (GET/HEAD any unmatched path)
CLI `dsh web` startup URL line and default-browser handoff (now carries ?token=)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/api/gateway/src/index.ts:194-201 (WebSocket /api/remote.mux upgrade in the gateway package, a separate transport into the Host API that calls connection.isTrustedRequest(req, 'trusted-host'))

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The WebSocket mux is an event/stream transport owned by the gateway package, already behind the same Host/Origin fence and never in PRIVILEGED_METHODS, so a solver can argue it carries no 'privileged' methods and is outside the /api configuration-plane bypass.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Non-index static assets and other named web routes must stay reachable without the browser session (the fix keeps them public); in particular the GitHub webhook route has its own HMAC signature check and must not be put behind browser-cookie auth, and the Host/Origin fence must still return 403 ahead of the new 401. A blanket gate at the webserver level breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: Fetch Headers object vs node:http header record (fix.diff:2344-2351)
plain HTTP request vs WebSocket upgrade request (fix.diff:1581-1584)
Cookie header with several ';'-separated segments; only the authority-derived cookie name is read (fix.diff:2395-2401)
repeated ?token= query parameters rejected; token accepted only on GET / (fix.diff:2502-2506)
Host header case/default-port variants normalized before cookie name and audience binding (fix.diff:2354-2361)
GET vs HEAD on the index (fix.diff:2580-2582)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second WebSocket upgrade route (e.g. a per-session event stream) gated only by connection.isTrustedRequest(req, 'trusted-host').
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The gateway already registers its own upgrade route using the Host/Origin helper; a maintainer adding a second stream path would copy that pattern without going through the /api route.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A plugin in another package registering a generic channel via ctx.connection.rpc.handle('/rpc', ...) whose handler reaches settings or session methods.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: rpc.handle is a public generic channel registry with no src caller at the pin; it exists so plugins can mount channels, and each channel gets its own route outside the /api handler.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A named exact route next to /plugins/events (e.g. a dev diagnostics or settings-export endpoint) that reaches Host state without the Connection check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Client plugins already register their own named webServer routes outside Connection; a dev or diagnostic route touching Host services is a plausible addition.

O9_family: missing authentication / security decision based on a client-controlled header (CWE-807, Host header treated as local authority)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap the Host-header loopback test for a TCP remoteAddress loopback check on PRIVILEGED_METHODS only (the alternative the fix's note rejects, fix.diff:371), leaving session.prompt, the generic channel, the interceptor and the WebSocket mux unauthenticated.

packages/webhook/webhook-github/src/index.ts:49-61 has its own HMAC check (handler.ts:92); not reviewed further.

Fairness concern (not a listed red flag): the published fix is a new authentication subsystem (276-line browser-auth.ts, launch token, signed authority-bound cookie, credential-store secret, CLI URL change). Hidden tests that bind to its specific API (authorizeIndex, authenticatedUrl, ?token= exchange, 401 vs 403 split, cookie naming) cannot be inferred from a short report unless the report specifies that contract; estimated effort is well above 45 minutes.
